label: Could lack an act: a contingent possession of an act in a respect
term: could lack its act in a respect (Lean `Lackability.CanLack`)
definition: Lackability.CanLack x r: x could be without its act in respect r. Explicitly identified PRIMITIVE predicate. Ordinary meaning: an iron could be cold, a stone could be at rest, so a hot iron and a moving stone have acts they could lack. At esse, the middle conjunct of PresentMomentHoldingReading says, one way, that whatever could lack being has received esse; it is not read as logical contingency in general. Distinguished from adopted potency POTENCY_1 (9f874532-f37e-590b-bec9-a9affb2762ac), which excludes act in the same respect: a thing in act in r can satisfy CanLack x r but not InPotency x r. Distinguished from capacity (DEF-CAPACITY-TO-BE), which concerns being able to be so, not being able to be otherwise.
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred. It carries the antecedent 'an actuality a thing could lack' of the respect-general concurrent-actualization premise.

formal_gap.meaning: Lackability.CanLack x r says that x could be without its act in r. The structure only supplies the predicate; nothing in Lean says when it holds, and it is not tied to a modal frame.
examples: A hot iron could be cold: it could lack its heat.
A thrown stone could be at rest: it could lack its motion.
exclusions: Being in potency in the adopted sense (able to be so and not actually so).
An act that its bearer could not be without, such as a necessary being's being, if there is one.
open_obligations: Its relation to a modal-logic contingency operator is not formalized.
That a thing with an act it could lack could lack being is the open premise LackableActBringsLackableBeing.
